test.name: Initialize project from objective text only — no FamilySearch tree ID
test.description: Single-turn decomposition: the user provides a research objective in detail but no FamilySearch person ID to seed the tree. Tests whether init-project can create a project with a minimal stub person built purely from the objective text. The init-project SKILL.md describes this as the bootstrap-sequence case where `subject_person_ids` may even be null at creation.

input.user_message: Start a new research project. I want to identify the maternal grandmother of Sarah Hennessy, who was born around 1920 in Boston, Massachusetts. Sarah's mother's maiden name was Mary Donovan but I don't know Mary's mother's name. No FamilySearch tree exists for any of these people yet.

judge_context: Should create a stub for Sarah Hennessy in tree.gedcomx.json (name, approximate birth year, place). Standardizing the user's stated 'Boston, Massachusetts' to a fuller form like 'Boston, Suffolk County, Massachusetts' is acceptable — it is place standardization of a stated fact, not fabrication
Should create a stub for Mary Donovan — her full name is stated and known; 'possibly' is not acceptable here. All confirmed information must appear in the tree from the start

Should create a stub for Mary Donovan's parent — surname Donovan (inferred from Mary's maiden name), which is a concrete identifying detail sufficient for stub creation. Sex is unspecified: assuming this is her father is the same unsound patrilineal assumption named in check-warnings/references/assumption-categories.md — do not credit 'father' language or a `sex` value asserted from the surname alone. The given name is unknown so it is spelled as the empty string (`given: ""`, never an omitted key — the schema requires the field), but a surname-only stub must be created so household searches can confirm this parent's identity

The maternal grandmother (Mary's mother, the research target) does NOT get a stub — her name is entirely unknown, so no concrete identifying detail exists. Creating a placeholder for her would be fabrication

Historical context in the pedigree analysis section (migration patterns, record availability, era context) is correct and expected per the skill spec — do not penalise it as fabrication. Fabrication means inventing facts about specific people (names, dates, places); historical background is analysis, not fabrication
Should NOT pretend to have data from a FamilySearch tree fixture — there is no person-read or tree fetch in this scenario; the skill must work from objective text alone

`person_search` is available and returns no candidates. Falling back to objective-text stubs is correct only after the search runs — judge whether the search was attempted, since a run that never searched and a run that searched and found nothing reach the same tree.

Should set `project.subject_person_ids` to the stub IDs that exist, OR to `null` (both are acceptable per research-schema-spec.md §1) — but should NOT include an ID for the unknown grandmother whose stub doesn't exist

The user volunteers family knowledge ('Sarah's mother's maiden name was Mary Donovan'). Recording this as a `known_holdings` entry with `holding_type: oral_knowledge`, linked via `relates_to_person_ids` to the Mary Donovan stub, is credited — dropping it entirely is the weaker outcome the holdings survey is meant to prevent. (Genealogist to confirm whether this should be required vs. merely credited for this single-turn case.)
